drhp.business: MRF manufactures and sells tyres for commercial vehicles, passenger vehicles, two-wheelers and tractors/farm equipment, selling both as an Original Equipment (OE) fitment to India's vehicle manufacturers and into the replacement market. The Company is a preferred OE fitment supplier to most of India's large OEMs, is fitted on most of India's top-selling passenger vehicles including next-generation EV models, and describes itself as the most preferred supplier of tyres to Electric Vehicles. It also exports tyres — including truck and light-truck radial, 3-wheeler and farm tyre categories — to …

drhp.expansion: The routed sections disclose no capacity additions, commissioning timelines or capex quantum for the tyre plants; expansion is described qualitatively rather than as a project pipeline. Geographic expansion is the main thread: the Company says it is strategically positioned to resume a strong growth trajectory in the year ahead 'driven primarily by targeted expansions in Africa, South East Asia and Europe', and new additions planned in the current year in the truck radial and farm radial categories are expected to significantly enhance business and market presence in Europe and the Americas, …

litigation.note: The Board states that during the year under review there were no material and significant orders passed by regulators, courts or tribunals impacting the going concern status or future operations, and that the auditors' and secretarial auditor's reports contain no qualification. The Company carries a provision for litigation and related disputes representing estimates mainly for probable claims arising out of litigation/disputes pending with authorities under various statutes (Goods and Service Tax, Excise and Customs Duty, Electricity/Fuel Surcharge, Cess); the probability and timing of any outflow depends on the final outcome of those litigations.

risks.note: The conflict in the middle east has raised commodity prices, with a risk premium likely to get added particularly to Crude; commodity prices are at an elevated level now which management says will impact margins in financial year 2026-27, and prices are expected to remain elevated for some time even after the conflict ends.
risks.risk: Raw material and commodity cost inflation

risks.note: Management states the world economy continues to be affected by geo political tensions and tariff related uncertainties, which will result in global slow down and impact demand in both domestic and export markets; the conflict has raised shipping costs and supply chain vulnerabilities, and the conflict in Iran caused substantial disruptions to the supply chain and to exports to the middle east, traditionally a very strong geography for the Company.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and supply-chain / freight disruption

risks.note: The Rupee depreciated 10% over the last year and 4% since the conflict began; rupee depreciation along with higher commodity costs can result in higher inflation, translate into higher interest rates and lower Government spending, and impact the economy negatively.

The forecast of a below normal monsoon is flagged as a negative that will impact the agricultural sector, rural demand and consumption — directly relevant given the tractor/farm tyre exposure — and all these could result in margin pressures for the tyre industry.
risks.risk: Below-normal monsoon and weak rural demand

risks.note: Uncertainty around United States tariffs continues, with global trade patterns shifting and geo economic fragmentation and geo political risks increasingly becoming a reality; global automakers, including European ones, face regulatory change, trade tension and uncertain economic outlook, which conditions demand for tyres.

Export momentum in the second half was constrained by economic challenges in the Philippines, political developments in Bangladesh and election cycles in select African nations, alongside the Middle East disruption — showing the export book's sensitivity to a handful of geographies.

Industrial relations were cordial except for a few instances of work disruption in the Arkonam, Tiruvottiyur and Trichy plants; long term settlements in the Trichy plants have not been completed and are under negotiation.

The tyre industry is undergoing rapid transformation driven by sustainability goals, electric mobility, digitalization and performance demands, requiring continuous technology absorption; regulatory compliance under R117 and AIS 142 standards obliges development of low rolling resistance and low-noise tyres without compromising safety and durability.
risks.risk: Regulatory and technology transition in tyres
